newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures close higher in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures close higher in lackluster trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher in lackluster trade as the market withstood the poor results of the U.S. Treasury's TIPS auction and the prospect of huge corporate supply, traders and analysts said.
"This is an impressive market," one T-bond futures trader said. "The underpinnings of this market are still intact."

Traders said the T-bond and Eurodollar futures market had factored in the auction results, noting the poor performance of the 10-year TIPS since their auction, and the difficulty for bond traders to hedge positions with Treasury Inflation Protected Securities (TIPS).

September T-bonds attempted to re-test 113-31/32 before and after the results of the five-year TIPS auction. The sale produced a high yield of 3.744 percent versus 3.715 percent in the when-issued market.
"Since this is the first one, there is a lot of indecision out there," one bond trader added.

He said the biggest negative factor for T-bonds was the corporate bond issuance. Philip Morris Cos Inc set a $1.0 billion eight-year bond, while another $2.5 billion in corporate bonds are slated to hit the high-yield market in the near term.
About $2.7 billion in new straight corporate high-grade debt was dumped on the market Tuesday.
September T-bonds rose to 114-03/32 in early morning trade amid expectations for a test of 114-08/32 and possibly 114-16/32 within the session.
Rumblings that South American countries may buy back Brady bonds contributed to the contract's decline to 113-20/32, from its fresh seven-month peak of 114-03/32, they said.
Peru's finance minister Jorge Camet said on RFTV on Wednesday that Peru had studied the possibility of repurchasing Brady bonds, but had not yet come to a decision.
Two U.S. institutions sold a total of 3,000 September T-bonds at 114-03/32, the seven-month high, soon after Camet's comments were reported.
However, September managed to limit losses above 113-19/32. Traders were preparing for a quick descent in prices if the contract edged below Tuesday's pit low of 113-12/32 and support at 113-11/32.
Total bond futures volume was extremely light, estimated at 225,000, traders said.
December Eurodollars also held above support at 94.02. Further support is seen at 93.99, traders said.
U.S. weekly jobless claims, which will be released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT Thursday, are forecast to rise to 341,000 against 332,000 in the prior week.

At the end of pit trade, September T-bonds were up 09/32 at 113-29/32, 10-year T-notes were 03/32 higher at 109-15/32, five-year notes were up 03/32 at 107-00, munibonds were 10/32 higher at 119-11/32 and December Eurodollars were up 0.01 at 94.07. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
